messages.subject: Meet and Analyze Data, Wed June 5th 3-5 PM - Bennett Conference Room CCAH - LAST SESSION BEFORE FALL QUARTER
messages.subject_clean: Meet and Analyze Data, Wed June 5th 3-5 PM - Bennett Conference Room CCAH - LAST SESSION BEFORE FALL QUARTER
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

we will be having a Meet and Analyze Data session from 3:00pm-5:00pm
today (05/29),
in the Bennett Conference Room at the Center for Companion Animal Health
(http://campusmap.ucdavis.edu/?b=33).
Hope to see you there!

This is also the last session before the Fall quarter (we won't run MAD
during Summer).

--

If you think you are going to join us, please let us know --

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeUW5QS55uDwDpusGYerY542D_tQubkmPMtUKlGdbmoSWfSSQ/viewform

--

Meet and Analyze Data (MAD) is a forum to bring your biological big
data and discuss high level concept problems (what is metagenome
assembly?) and low level coding problems (what does this error message
even mean?!) and everything in between. There is no scheduled or
specific activity: people show up with questions about how to analyze
their data, or maybe they are willing to help others. We typically get
questions about experimental design for
transcriptomic/metagenomic/genomic projects, or how to install
software, or how to run their analysis on clusters or the cloud.

Cheers,
Luiz Irber

Hope to see folks tomorrow!

messages.subject: Looking for carpentry instructors/helpers
messages.body_plain:
Hello D-ruggers & DSI affiliates,

I am going to be hosting a Data Carpentry workshop using the Social Science course material in 2 weeks, June 19-20 at Chico State. I am expecting about 15-20 participants but I could go up to as much 30 without being too crammed (or having to find an different room)
https://csucdsi.github.io/2019-06-19-chicostate/

I am looking for an additional instructor and any helpers that are interested. This is a self-organized workshop, so I can't fund any travel reimbursement. I do have an open room in my house that I would be happy to put someone up in, and I can cover meals but that's about the limit of the budget. I did submit the workshop request to the Carpentries, but I'm not sure how much they'll help with recruitment of instructors/helpers since it's self-organized.

Please let me know if you're interested & available.
Also you are encouraged to pass this information on to anyone that you think may be interested in helping.

Thank you!
-Robin

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Binned data, finding 25% of total and finding in which bin is this 25% total (new to R)
messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: Binned data, finding 25% of total and finding in which bin is this 25% total (new to R)
messages.body_plain:
An approach could be to compute percentage then use cumulative sum (cumsum), then subset for first row with cumulated percentage >=25%. You might want to use arrange() for pre-sorting, and group_by if you have multiple groups

library(tidyverse)
df<- data.frame(bin = seq(1, 20, by=4), count = c(7,5,2,6,9)) %>%
  mutate(perc = 100* count/sum(count),
         perc_cumul = cumsum(perc))

df
#>   bin count      perc perc_cumul
#> 1   1     7 24.137931   24.13793
#> 2   5     5 17.241379   41.37931
#> 3   9     2  6.896552   48.27586
#> 4  13     6 20.689655   68.96552
#> 5  17     9 31.034483  100.00000

df %>%
  filter(perc_cumul>=25) %>%
  head(1)
#>   bin count     perc perc_cumul
#> 1   5     5 17.24138   41.37931
<sup>Created on 2019-06-13 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>
